assessment.nobel_worthiness: Converts small molecules into inducers of proximity, hijacking E3 ligases to destroy targets once considered undruggable. This is a genuinely new chemical modality, with a design logic (heterobifunctional linkers, glue-like surface remodeling) that gives precise control over recognition, which is what I value most. It has changed what chemists and clinicians can attempt against scaffolding proteins and transcription factors.
assessment.attribution: PROTAC concept and first proof (Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto) and the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type glues (Handa, Ito) are separate threads; a three-person prize spanning both is plausible. Ciulli and Gray have major later contributions that the cap may force out.
assessment.maturity: Large clinical pipeline and multiple late-stage trials; mechanistic understanding of cereblon-based degradation is well confirmed across independent labs. Timing seems ripe, though approvals of a designed degrader are still maturing.
uncertainties: Division of credit between PROTAC inventors and the thalidomide-mechanism discoverers is unresolved.
Clinical benefit of designed degraders is not yet fully established; my recollection of trial status is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry that made siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines deliverable; the pKa-tuned lipid design that is neutral in circulation and cationic in the endosome is a clear molecular design principle with enormous real-world impact. It is a textbook case of a chemical discovery changing what clinicians can do.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the foundational lipid-nanoparticle and ionizable-lipid formulation work; Anderson and Langer developed lipidoid libraries; MacLachlan, Hope and Madden contributed formulation and process steps. Many hands, so any three-person split is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Validated at global scale in approved siRNA therapy and COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, with independent confirmation. The 2023 Medicine Prize recognized the mRNA side but not the delivery chemistry, which leaves the delivery chemistry timely.
uncertainties: Possible perception of overlap with the 2023 Medicine award on mRNA.
Credit among Cullis, Anderson, Langer, MacLachlan, Hope and Madden is complicated by industry and patent history that I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors are chemically engineered proteins that perform deaminase chemistry on DNA at a programmed site without double-strand breaks. This is molecular design with precise control, and it has spread throughout biomedicine and agriculture; first therapeutic use makes translation tangible.
assessment.attribution: Liu's lab made the decisive contributions, with Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, requiring directed evolution of a new deaminase) as lead inventors. Nishida and Kondo reported an independent deaminase-based approach. The Liu-led trio is natural, but CRISPR itself was already honored (2020).
assessment.maturity: Rapidly and independently reproduced, with first-in-human clinical applications. Interpretation is stable; the long-term safety record is still short.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as chemistry or as a downstream application of the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Independent contribution of Nishida and Kondo may complicate a clean three-person allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics turned protein identification and quantification into a routine, systems-level chemical measurement. Shotgun proteomics, quantitative labeling and targeted/DIA strategies underpin biomarker discovery and the readouts of modern biosensing and clinical research. Broad, lasting, enabling impact on biology and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution quantitative proteomics, SILAC), Aebersold (ICAT, SRM and SWATH) and Yates (shotgun/MudPIT) are widely seen as the central figures. Hunt, Gygi and Heck have strong claims too, so exclusion is painful. Ionization (Fenn, Tanaka) was recognized in 2002.
assessment.maturity: Mature, universally adopted and continuously confirmed; timing is long overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Attribution is crowded and the enabling ionization prizes were earlier, so the incremental claim may appear to be a technology extension.
Relative weighting of Hunt, Gygi and Heck against the three proposed is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and single-electron pathways with mild conditions, and it is used in drug discovery and in bioconjugation and labeling chemistry. It has changed the routine toolbox of synthetic chemists.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and MacMillan reported the founding 2008-2009 demonstrations; Nicewicz, König, Fukuzumi and Melchiorre contributed key mechanistic and conceptual advances. MacMillan is already a laureate (2021), which may argue against including him.
assessment.maturity: Very widely reproduced and industrially adopted; the field is mature, though how fundamental the principle is relative to prior photochemistry is debated.
uncertainties: Prior-laureate status of MacMillan complicates the trio.
Priority claims dating to earlier photochemistry (Fukuzumi, Kellogg, Cano-Yelo and Deronzier) are not resolved in my knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets chemists install new functional groups at defined positions in proteins in living cells, through orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs. It gives exquisite site-specific control over protein chemistry, which is important for biophysical probes, bioorthogonal handles and protein therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the approach in bacteria and eukaryotes; Chin extended it to multicellular organisms, quadruplet codons and recoded genomes; Wang contributed key early work. Mehl and Yokoyama are also credited, so the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Replicated in many laboratories and applied broadly; therapeutic use (e.g. site-specific antibody conjugates) is progressing. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Credit distribution among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama is uncertain.
Overlap with the 2018 directed-evolution and 2023-related protein engineering recognitions could weigh against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single molecules electrically and enabled portable DNA/RNA sequencing; the idea of a molecular-scale sensor with single-molecule resolution is exactly the biosensing principle that spreads to broader analytes. Protein engineering of pores (Bayley) was crucial for practical sensing.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton conceived strand-translocation sequencing; Bayley engineered alpha-hemolysin and sensing; Akeson and Kasianowicz demonstrated polynucleotide detection. Boundary between concept, demonstration and the commercial device (Oxford Nanopore) is complicated.
assessment.maturity: Technology is in wide use and independently validated, including for long-read sequencing, although accuracy and applications are still evolving. Timing is plausible.
uncertainties: Four-to-six-way credit dispute; a three-person limit is hard.
Whether the committee values the sensor concept or the finished sequencing instrument.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed nanoparticle assembly and spherical nucleic acids give programmable, sequence-encoded control over nanoparticle architecture, and they enabled colorimetric diagnostics and intracellular gene regulation. It resembles my own area of nanoparticle-biomolecule hybrids, which I treat as a source of bias and discount accordingly.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin and Alivisatos independently published the first DNA-nanoparticle assembly papers in 1996; Mirkin extended the work to spherical nucleic acids and diagnostics. Storhoff and Mucic were key coauthors rather than leaders.
assessment.maturity: Established in the laboratory and in some commercial diagnostics, but clinical translation of spherical nucleic acids as therapeutics has been limited so far. Somewhat less mature than the higher-ranked entries.
uncertainties: Alivisatos's contribution is more to the nanocrystal field generally, so his inclusion is uncertain.
My familiarity with the topic could bias my assessment.
